items.stem: A script that lives inside and is attached to a specific Google Sheet is best described as which kind of Apps Script project?

options.rationale: Correct: a bound script is attached to a specific host document.
A standalone script is not attached to a specific document.
Apps Script projects are not browser extensions.
Apps Script is not compiled to a standalone binary.

items.explanation: Correct: a bound script is attached to a specific host document.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make an Apps Script Sheets automation more reliable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Read and write ranges in bulk rather than cell by cell
options.rationale: Correct: bulk operations are far faster and avoid quota issues.

options.text: Be mindful of per-service daily quotas
options.rationale: Correct: services such as email have daily limits.

options.text: Request the broadest possible authorization scopes
options.rationale: Narrow scopes are safer; broad scopes over-permission the script.

options.text: Loop one cell at a time for large sheets
options.rationale: Cell-by-cell access is slow and can hit limits.

items.explanation: Correct: bulk range access and quota awareness improve reliability.

items.stem: You want a script to run automatically every Monday morning without anyone opening the sheet. What should you use?

options.rationale: Correct: a time-based trigger runs on a schedule with the needed authorization.
onOpen only runs when the document is opened and cannot perform authorized actions.

options.text: A manual menu click each week

options.rationale: A formula cannot send email or run on a schedule.

items.explanation: Correct: a time-based trigger runs on a schedule with the needed authorization.
